findings.explanation: Splunkbase ID 3185 is the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft IIS, not Proofpoint On Demand.
findings.quote:
"title": "Splunkbase — Splunk Add-on for Proofpoint On Demand",
      "url": "https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/3185"
findings.suggested_fix: Update the URL and reference to point to the correct Proofpoint add-on on Splunkbase.

findings.explanation: The implementation section consists of generic template scaffolding with literal ellipsis placeholders (`index=...`) and non-domain fields.
findings.quote: Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`host, user, action`).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace boilerplate with explicit Proofpoint spam score threshold configuration, quarantine release logging setup, and ticketing correlation steps.

findings.explanation: The explanation mentions URL rewriting and DLP rather than false-positive spam and content filter rate tracking.
findings.quote: We watch how Proofpoint treats and rewrites mail, so threats and DLP events line up with what the security team already sees in their console.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain in plain terms how we monitor when legitimate business emails are mistakenly blocked as junk or spam.

summary: The use case points to the Microsoft IIS add-on (Splunkbase 3185) for Proofpoint, contains generic unfilled boilerplate across detailedImplementation, and misinterprets the SPL time window (-30d) as a threshold in prose.
